topic: Testing domain-to-HTTP exception mappings with MockMvc
tomorrowTopic: Consolidating validation and domain failures into one stable API error contract

hook.headline: Test the boundary, not the exception class
hook.hook: A domain failure can be correct while its REST mapping is wrong. MockMvc lets you exercise Spring MVC request handling and assert the HTTP contract produced by your exception advice.
hook.visualCaption: request → controller/service → domain failure → advice → ProblemDetail

mentalModel.title: Exercise the whole MVC mapping path
mentalModel.coreIdea: The useful test starts with an HTTP request and observes the response. That verifies controller routing, exception resolution, your @RestControllerAdvice mapping, ProblemDetail rendering, and the status seen by the client.
mentalModel.keyOutcome: The test protects the public error contract rather than only the implementation of the mapper.
mentalModel.mentalShortcut: if clients depend on it, assert it at the HTTP boundary

code.title: Assert the observable contract
code.intro: Trigger the failure through MockMvc and verify what a real MVC client would observe.
code.highlightReason: ProblemDetail responses are intended to render with the problem media type, so the representation is part of the API contract worth asserting.
code.takeaway: Drive the failure through Spring MVC; do not reduce the test to calling the advice method directly.
code.professionalNote: MockMvc performs Spring MVC request handling with mock request and response objects rather than a running server. Ensure the test configuration contains both the controller path and the relevant advice.

production.title: Catch broken mappings before integration
production.scenario: A refactor preserves OrderNotFound but accidentally removes or changes the MVC exception mapping. Domain unit tests still pass while REST clients receive a different response.
problems: Testing only the service proves the domain failure, not its HTTP translation.
Testing only the advice method can miss whether Spring MVC actually selects that handler for the request path.
production.professionalApproach: Keep domain behavior covered with domain/service tests, then add a focused MockMvc test for each important public error mapping. Assert stable client-facing fields and avoid coupling tests to incidental internals.
production.debugClue: If the service test passes but MockMvc returns an unexpected status or body, inspect exception-handler selection and the MVC test configuration before changing domain logic.

interview.question: Why use MockMvc instead of directly unit-testing an @ExceptionHandler method?
interview.answer: A direct unit test proves the mapper method returns the expected object, but it does not prove Spring MVC will route a real request failure to that handler or render the expected response. MockMvc exercises MVC request handling with mock HTTP objects, so it is better suited to verifying the boundary contract. Keep separate unit tests for domain behavior when they add value.
remember: domain tests prove business failure semantics
MockMvc proves Spring MVC translation and response shape
assert stable client-visible fields, not incidental implementation details
